content.hero_subtitle: The industry-standard IEEE 802.3 CRC checksum generator
content.p1: CRC-32B is the most widely used variant of the CRC-32 family, employing the IEEE 802.3 polynomial (0x04C11DB7). It is the standard checksum in Ethernet networking, ZIP archives, PNG images, and countless other protocols. When people refer to 'CRC-32' in practice, they almost always mean CRC-32B. This tool generates the exact same checksums used by WinZip, 7-Zip, and network hardware worldwide.
content.what_desc: CRC-32B uses the generator polynomial 0x04C11DB7, standardized by IEEE 802.3 for Ethernet. The 'B' suffix distinguishes it from other CRC-32 variants using different polynomials. It provides the same mathematical guarantees as CRC-32 but is the de facto standard for modern applications, making it the most compatible choice.

content.warning_desc: CRC-32B is a checksum, not a cryptographic hash. While excellent for detecting accidental corruption, it provides no security against intentional data manipulation. Use SHA-256 or SHA-512 for cryptographic security.

faq.q1: Should I use CRC-32 or CRC-32B?
faq.a1: Use CRC-32B. It's the IEEE 802.3 standard and is what most software and hardware implementations use. When documentation says 'CRC-32' without qualification, they typically mean CRC-32B.
faq.a2: Yes. CRC-32B uses the same IEEE 802.3 polynomial as ZIP, gzip, PNG, and virtually all standard tools.
faq.a3: CRC-32B has stronger error detection, especially for short data blocks. Adler-32 is faster in software but less reliable for data under 1000 bytes.
